Check whether a contrast has enough distinct label shuffles for a NOPE.

Source: R/compare-group-compositions.R
has_enough_shuffles_for_nope.Rd

Each NOPE edge is the nope_quantile of its statistic (\(R\) or \(E\)) across label shuffles, so it only works as a bar when the true grouping is a small fraction of all shuffles. With few subjects there are few distinct ways to split them; the true split then sets the quantile itself and neither statistic can clear it, the same limit that keeps a 3 versus 3 permutation p-value at or above 0.1.

Usage

has_enough_shuffles_for_nope(contrast_group, nope_quantile = 0.95)

Arguments

contrast_group

Factor of group labels for one contrast.

nope_quantile

Quantile of each shuffled statistic used as its NOPE edge.

Value

TRUE when \(R\) and \(E\) can clear their NOPEs, FALSE otherwise.

Details

\(R\) and \(E\) depend only on which subjects share a group, so relabelings that swap two equal-sized groups count as one split. The number of distinct splits is n! / (prod(n_g!) * prod(m_k!)), where n_g are group sizes and m_k counts groups of each size (10 for 3 versus 3, 35 for 4 versus 4). The contrast passes when the true split is under 1 - nope_quantile of all shuffles, i.e. more than 20 distinct splits at the default 0.95. Depends only on group sizes, so it uses no random numbers and runs once per contrast.
